headline: MARIMACA COPPER MAKES TSX TOP GAINER — PAMPA MEDINA HITS 216m AT 1.0% Cu AND 7.2g/t Ag; HIGH-GRADE CORE: 62m AT 2.2% Cu, 21.5g/t Ag
snippet: Marimaca Copper Corp. (TSX: MARI, ASX: MC2) reported drillhole SPRD-15 at the Pampa Medina deposit in Chile's Antofagasta Region returned 216 metres at 1.0% Cu and 7.2 g/t Ag from 466 metres, including 62 metres at 2.2% Cu and 21.5 g/t Ag from 602 metres — sending MARI to the TSX's top gainer list on September 8, 2026, with copper trading above $14,600 per tonne. Step-out holes SPRD-12, SPD-13, and SPRD-17 have extended mineralization 300 metres south and west of the central corridor, expanding the defined 3km × 1.5km area of interest; the mineralised sediment horizon's continuity both horizontally and vertically across the full system makes Pampa Medina one of the more compelling undeveloped copper-silver systems in the Americas at today's record copper prices.

headline: DPM METALS EXPANDS TO 15 DRILL RIGS AT ČOKA RAKITA — 246m AT 1.36% CuEq FROM DUMITRU POTOK; CAMP ALREADY HOSTS 2.6Moz Au AND 1.9B LBS Cu INFERRED
snippet: DPM Metals Inc. (TSX: DPM, ASX: DPM) reported on September 8, 2026 that drillhole BIDD253 at the Dumitru Potok prospect on Serbia's Čoka Rakita licence returned 246 metres at 1.36% copper equivalent (0.67% Cu, 0.69 g/t Au, 4.21 g/t Ag) from 1,377 metres, extending marble-hosted intrusive skarn mineralization 90 metres west and 100 metres southwest of the known resource — plus encouraging results 300 metres to the north at shallow levels. The company is expanding its 2026 program by 12,000–15,000 metres to a total of 32,000–35,000 metres, with eight rigs currently operating and a target of 15 rigs on site by year-end. The Čoka Rakita Rakita Camp already hosts an inferred mineral resource of 2.6 million ounces of gold and 1.9 billion pounds of copper — still growing in multiple open directions.

headline: JAPAN'S JOGMEC BACKS ACLARA'S BRAZIL HEAVY RARE EARTH PLAY — $3M EARN-IN SECURES 30% OPTION IN IONIC CLAY PROJECT AS CHINA'S NOV DEADLINE LOOMS
snippet: Aclara Resources Inc. (TSX: ARA) entered a joint venture agreement with Japan's state metals security agency JOGMEC on September 8, 2026, giving JOGMEC the option to acquire a 30% interest in one of Aclara's Brazilian heavy rare earth ionic clay exploration projects in exchange for sole-funding up to US$3.0 million of exploration over a three-year earn-in period — extendable by one year for an additional US$1.5 million. The deal is strategically timed as China's enhanced rare earth export control suspension approaches its November 2026 reset: JOGMEC's mandate to secure Japan's strategic mineral supply puts a government-backed buyer of record behind the ionic clay-hosted NdPr and heavy REE model, validating the project class for broader institutional investors tracking Western supply chain buildout.

headline: EUREKA METALS HITS 36.9% TiO2 AT TYEE — NINE SAMPLES TOP 35% AT QUÉBEC TITANIUM PROJECT ADJACENT TO RIO TINTO'S PRODUCING LAC TIO MINE
snippet: Eureka Metals Corp. (CSE: ERKA) reported five new high-grade titanium occurrences at its 100%-owned Tyee Titanium Project in Québec on September 8, 2026, with nine grab samples returning more than 35% TiO₂ and a peak of 36.87% TiO₂ — plus vanadium credits of 0.26%–0.30% V₂O₅ in each. High-grade results span multiple new areas of the project beyond historically known zones, indicating a materially underexplored footprint. Tyee sits 65 km north of Rio Tinto's producing Lac Tio ilmenite mine in the Havre-Saint-Pierre Anorthosite Complex — the world's largest high-grade titanium district — with Eureka's maiden drill program now being planned to test the subsurface continuation of the surface occurrences.

headline: STANMORE SEIZES 724Mt COKING COAL BLOCK FOR US$105M — MORANBAH SOUTH EXPANDS QUEENSLAND EMPIRE ADJACENT TO EAGLE DOWNS
snippet: Stanmore Resources (ASX: SMR) agreed to acquire 100% of the Moranbah South metallurgical coal tenements in Queensland's Bowen Basin from Exxaro Resources for US$105 million ($145 million AUD) on September 8, 2026 — adding 724 million tonnes of measured and indicated premium hard coking coal immediately adjacent to Stanmore's Eagle Downs and Isaac Downs Extension projects in a potential mine-infrastructure sharing scenario. The deal simultaneously extinguishes up to US$60 million of deferred and contingent consideration under a 2024 designated area agreement, enhancing Eagle Downs' net economics. Exxaro first acquired Anglo American's 50% stake via pre-emptive rights before flowing the entire tenement to Stanmore, with final close expected before year-end subject to FIRB and ACCC approval.

headline: URANIUM TERM PRICES HIT 18-YEAR HIGH AT $94/LB — KAZATOMPROM'S THIRD CONSECUTIVE GUIDANCE CUT CEMENTS STRUCTURAL SUPPLY DEFICIT
snippet: The uranium long-term benchmark reached $94 per pound in September 2026 — an 18-year high — as Kazatomprom issued its third consecutive downward production revision, flagging a TQZ sulphuric acid plant delay that is compressing in-situ leaching capacity, while Cameco disclosed delivery obligations of 29–32 million pounds against own production of just 19.5–21.5 million pounds, requiring purchases to bridge the gap. Spot uranium settled near $89.50–$90 per pound, and the five-year forward curve prices uranium at $108 per pound. The World Nuclear Association's updated reactor requirement forecast projects demand more than doubling by 2040 — driven by SMR construction, U.S. plant restarts, and new data-centre power agreements — while primary mine supply is demonstrably unable to respond at current incentive prices.

headline: BRIEN LUNDIN: WALL STREET HAS NAMED THE DEBASEMENT TRADE — $40T U.S. DEBT MAKES GOLD'S BULL MARKET STRUCTURAL, NOT CYCLICAL
snippet: Brien Lundin, editor of The Gold Newsletter, argues in a September 5, 2026 Money Metals podcast transcript that gold has entered its durable institutional phase — Wall Street now openly calls the rally the 'debasement trade,' acknowledging that U.S. federal debt above $40 trillion cannot be serviced with sustained real rates without triggering a fiscal crisis that makes the tightening self-defeating. Lundin's key insight for mining investors: the same debt math that caps the Fed's ability to hike also underpins commodity-denominated assets including physical metals and mining equities, meaning CPI-driven mining stock selloffs are now buying opportunities within the structural trade rather than evidence that the cycle has ended — a framework directly relevant to positioning around Thursday's August CPI release and the September 16 FOMC decision.

headline: INDIANS DEFY MODI'S GOLD BAN — IMPORTS DOUBLED TO 40-45t IN JULY DESPITE 15% DUTY; $71.98B RECORD FY2025-26 AS FESTIVAL SEASON BUILDS
snippet: India's Prime Minister renewed his appeal on September 1, 2026 for citizens to stop buying gold for one year — backed by a customs duty increase from 6% to 15% — in response to a merchandise trade deficit that topped $330 billion in FY2025-26 and gold imports that hit a record US$71.98 billion in the same period, 24% above the prior year. The response: Indian gold imports doubled in July to an estimated 40–45 tonnes after two weak months, and the festival and wedding season that historically drives Q4 demand is now building. The data underscores the structural floor for global gold demand — 87% of Indian households own gold, cultural buying patterns have historically outpaced every government intervention attempt, and sovereign demand from China and Russia is now layered above India's structural baseline.
